Systems Library

Offense 11

4-Out 1-In Ball-Screen Continuity (Villanova / Jay Wright) Family: spread ball-screen offense with one post player. The dominant U Sports / NCAA / NBA framework today. 5-Out Motion / Modern Spread Family: spaced motion with no traditional post; everyone can pass, dribble, shoot. Continuity Ball-Screen Offense Family: ball-screen offense that flows from one ball-screen into another automatically — no reset needed. Dribble-Drive Motion (Vance Walberg → John Calipari) Family: spread offense built around penetrate-and-kick. No traditional post. Lane is open by design. Flex Offense Family: continuity offense built on the flex cut (baseline cut off a back-screen) and a down-screen for the screener. Horns Set Family Family: set-play family (not a system) — extremely common in college and pro. Two bigs at the elbows, two shooters in the corners, PG up top. Motion Offense (Bob Knight / Indiana lineage) Family: read-and-react continuity. No called plays — players make decisions based on rules and reads. Princeton Offense (Pete Carril) Family: continuity motion with heavy use of back-cuts, ball reversal, and high-post passing. Read-and-React (Rick Torbett) Family: layered motion / decision-tree system. Replaces called plays with 20+ "layers" of conditioned reactions to teammate actions. Spread Pick-and-Roll (Modern NBA) Family: the modern NBA's default offense — empty-side or middle ball-screen with maximum spacing. Triangle Offense (Tex Winter) Family: continuity / read-and-react half-court system organized around a strong-side triangle (corner, wing, post).

Defense 10

1-3-1 Zone / Trap Defense Family: disrupting zone — one at the top, three across the FT line, one at the rim. 2-3 Zone Defense Family: zone — two players at the top of the key, three across the baseline. Drop Coverage (Ball-Screen Defense) Family: ball-screen defensive scheme — the most common coverage in basketball. Full-Court Press Defenses Family: disrupting full-court pressure — used in spurts to force turnovers, change tempo, and tire the offense. ICE / Blue (Ball-Screen Defense) Family: side ball-screen coverage. ICE = "Force the ball away from the screen, toward the baseline." Match-Up Zone Defense Family: hybrid zone / man — defenders start in zone positions but match up to a man as they enter their area. No-Middle Defense Family: half-court man-to-man — every drive forced to the baseline or sideline, never to the middle. Pack-Line Defense (Dick Bennett → Tony Bennett) Family: half-court man-to-man variant. Conservative, gap-oriented, deny-the-paint philosophy. Scram Switch One-line: A defensive call where a help defender re-switches to fix a mismatch created by an earlier switch. Switch-Everything Defense Family: modern man-to-man. Switch every screen — on-ball, off-ball, all of them.

Transition 1

Transition Offense — Numbered Break + Early Offense Score before the defense is set. Most efficient possessions in basketball happen in the first 7 seconds of the shot clock.

Concepts 6

Ball-Screen Reads (Concept Reference) The ball-handler has 5 reads on every ball-screen. Coverage determines which one. Closeouts (Concept Reference) How a defender approaches a shooter who has just received the ball. Cuts (Concept Reference) Every cut a coach should know by name. Off-Ball Screens (Concept Reference) The screen types every coach should be able to identify on film and defend by name. Spacing (Concept Reference) Two passes away = a defender should be in the gap, not on the man. Zone Attack (Concept Reference) How to attack any zone — 2-3, 1-3-1, match-up, 3-2.

Actions 7

Chicago Action One-line: Pin-down → dribble hand-off (DHO). Cousin of zoom but starts with a pin instead of a down-screen. Get Action One-line: PG passes to a wing, then sprints to set a ball-screen for that wing. Hammer Action One-line: A baseline-driving guard kicks to a weak-side corner shooter who just used a back-screen ("hammer screen"). Iverson Cut One-line: A wing cuts ACROSS the FT line off two elbow screens to receive the ball on the opposite wing. Ram Screen One-line: A screen-the-screener action: a small player screens for the screening big BEFORE the big screens for the ball. Spain Pick-and-Roll (Action Reference) One-line: Ball-screen + a back-screen on the dropping big's defender. The roller is unguarded. Zoom Action One-line: Down-screen → dribble hand-off (DHO). Two screens in one action for a shooter.

Special Situations 1

BLOB / SLOB / ATO Playbook (Special Situations) Special situations are 5–10% of possessions but 15–20% of margin in close games. Coaches who win the SS battle win more 1-possession games.
